market_context: United States/general English; fresh and cooked shrimp spoilage signs
title: How to tell if shrimp has gone bad

seo.title: How to tell if shrimp is bad: smell and texture signs
seo.meta_description: Fresh shrimp should have firm, clear or pearl-like flesh with little odor. Sour, rancid, strongly fishy or ammonia odor is a clear discard sign.
seo.search_intent: Recognize shrimp spoilage and know when shrimp should not be eaten.

excerpt: FDA describes fresh shrimp as having clear, pearl-like flesh with little or no odor. Spoiled seafood can develop sour, rancid, fishy or ammonia odors, which may become stronger during cooking. Storage time still matters: raw seafood should be cooked or frozen within 1–2 refrigerated days.
content_html:
Shrimp can smell mildly of the sea, but it should not smell like ammonia or aggressively fishy. FDA describes fresh shrimp flesh as clear, pearl-like and firm, with little or no odor.

Odor is an important warning

FDA says spoiled seafood can develop sour, rancid, fishy or ammonia-like odors, which often become stronger after cooking.

If cooked seafood gives off either a fleeting or persistent ammonia odor, FDA says not to eat it.

Texture provides another clue

Fresh shrimp should feel firm. Very soft, mushy or distinctly slimy flesh—especially combined with abnormal odor—is more concerning than color alone.

Color by itself is not enough

Species, handling, cooking and pigment changes can alter shrimp color. Dark spotting can also arise from melanosis without automatically meaning bacterial spoilage, so odor, texture and storage history matter more.

Respect storage time even when it looks normal

USDA recommends keeping raw fish and shellfish only 1–2 days at 40 °F or below before cooking or freezing.

What to look for when buying

Choose refrigerated shrimp or shrimp displayed on plenty of fresh ice. Avoid frozen packages that are open, damaged or full of large ice crystals suggesting long storage or thaw-refreeze cycles.

Bottom line

Sour, rancid or ammonia-like odor is a strong discard signal. Combine smell with texture, cold-chain history and storage time, and never taste suspicious shrimp as a test.

faq.question: What should fresh shrimp smell like?
faq.answer: Very mild or nearly odorless, not sour, rancid, strongly fishy or ammonia-like.

faq.question: Is mushy shrimp spoiled?
faq.answer: Fresh flesh should be firm. Very mushy or slimy texture, especially with off odor, is concerning.

faq.question: How long does raw shrimp last refrigerated?
faq.answer: USDA recommends cooking or freezing raw shellfish within 1–2 days at 40 °F or below.
